identity: A short children's comic-strip / illustrated story page in simple MSA, Gulf character names. Token 0-3 is the title line ('Mouza the darling and her brother Rashoud'); the remaining five <NL>-delimited lines are speech balloons of a sibling dialogue in front of a pet-shop window: 'look at this shop's display' / 'ornamental birds - how I'd love to own a canary' / 'nice idea, you'll enjoy its song' / 'but I hate seeing a bird caged' / 'birds have the right to stay free above the trees'. Register is child-directed dialogue with a closing moral; utterances are short and each balloon carries one or two of them.
law: The sentence unit here is the single independent predication = one complete utterance act. Because each balloon is short, most lines are exactly one sentence, so the mandatory paragraph-final boundaries carry most of the load. INSIDE a line a boundary falls only where two syntactically independent predications are juxtaposed with NO connective, no subordinator and no shared argument - in this register that means a short verbless exclamative/evaluative fragment (a naming or a reaction: 'tuyur zina', 'fikra latifa') followed by a full clause that cannot take it as an argument. Everything that is grammatically bound to what precedes stays inside the sentence: a clause opened by a connective (wa-lakinnani), an 'an-complement (an ara, an tabqa), and adjectival or locative tails (mahbusan dakhil qafas saghir; hurra taliqa fawq al-ashjar). A title line is one unit. <NL> itself never carries a boundary.

Mandatory (pre-<NL> and final) boundaries: 3 rashud, 9 al-mahall, 18 kanari, 23 bi-taghridih, 33 saghir, 43 al-ashjar. Two internal sites are genuinely contestable and I split both. SITE 1, i=12 (zina): 'tuyur zina' is a verbless nominal exclamation - either the shop label read aloud or the child naming what she sees - and 'kam arghab fi iqtina' usfur kanari' is a complete kam-exclamative with its own first-person subject; it cannot govern 'tuyur zina' as subject, object or apposition, and nothing links them. Discovery followed by wish = two acts, so a boundary at 12. SITE 2, i=21 (latifa): structurally the same shape - 'fikra latifa' is khabar of an elided 'hadhihi', a complete verbless reply, and 'sa-tastamti' bi-taghridih' is an independent future clause addressed to the sibling. Evaluation followed by prediction = two acts, boundary at 21. Treating 12 and 21 alike is forced by consistency: identical fragment+clause geometry must get identical treatment. Confidence on both is 'med' rather than 'hi' for one reason only: Arabic print is comma-heavy and the source could have used a comma splice ('tuyur zina, kam arghab') instead of the exclamation mark or ellipsis a comic balloon normally takes; the syntax says split, the punctuation convention is the residual risk. Sites I considered and rejected: i=25 'wa-lakinnani' opens with a connective and is already line-initial, so no invented break precedes it and none follows inside its line - 'akrahu an ara usfuran mahbusan dakhil qafas saghir' is one predication with an 'an-complement plus hal and locative tails. i=39/41 in the last line: 'al-tuyur min haqqiha an tabqa hurra taliqa fawq al-ashjar' is topic + predicate with an 'an-complement; 'hurra taliqa' are two coordinate adjectives on tabqa and 'fawq al-ashjar' is its locative, so no split before them. i=5-9 'unzuri ila wajihat hadha al-mahall' is a single imperative. The title (0-3) is a single noun phrase, one unit.
